about.title: Sunnyvale Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You are more worried about the wrist you landed on or the embarrassment of going down in a crowded aisle. But in Sunnyvale, where daily life runs through the shopping centers along El Camino Real, the properties near SR-237, and the apartment complexes off Mathilda and Fair Oaks Avenues, property conditions matter, and California law puts a duty on the people who control those spaces. If a wet floor, broken step, or unlit walkway caused your injury, the central question becomes notice: did the owner know about the hazard, or should they have known, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? Proving that usually depends on evidence that disappears quickly, including surveillance footage, incident reports, and the hazard itself before someone mops it up. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that matches Sunnyvale residents with an independent premises liability attorney who works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Sunnyvale Residents Turn to LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice Is the Heart of Your Case
items.desc: California requires you to show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and did nothing. An attorney in our network knows how to dig into cleaning logs, maintenance records, and prior complaints to build that picture.

items.title: Video and Evidence Vanish Fast
items.desc: Many Sunnyvale stores and complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days. Connecting early means a preservation letter can go out before the footage of your fall is gone for good.

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: Most California premises claims carry a two-year limit, but a fall on city or other public property in Sunnyvale can trigger a much shorter government claim window. Understanding which clock applies to you is one of the first things an attorney will sort out.

items.question: I fell on a public sidewalk in Sunnyvale. Is that different from falling in a store?
items.answer: Yes, and the difference matters a great deal. When the property belongs to the City of Sunnyvale, Santa Clara County, or another public entity, California generally requires a formal government claim within six months of the injury, not the two years that apply to private owners. Missing that window can end the case before it starts, so acting quickly is essential.

items.question: The store says I wasn't watching where I was going. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not under California law. The state follows pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by whatever share of blame is assigned to you, but it is not eliminated. Even if a jury decided you were partly distracted, the owner could still be responsible for their portion if they failed to address a hazard they should have known about.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall in Sunnyvale?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if the pain seems manageable, because fall injuries often worsen over the following days. Photograph the exact spot, the hazard, your footwear, and any missing warning signs, and ask the property manager for a copy of any incident report. Then request in writing that surveillance video be preserved, since many businesses along El Camino Real and Mathilda Avenue record over their footage quickly.
